hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Vedanta Iron And Steel Limited (VISL) — demerged from the Vedanta group effective 1 May 2026 — as "a leading ferrous resources company" with a diversified India-and-Africa portfolio of iron ore mining and steelmaking assets under the tagline "Strengthening Foundations, Building Nations".

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Described as "a leading ferrous resources company supplying the materials that form the foundations of modern economies" through exploration, mining and production of iron ore and high-quality steel.
- Operations span India and Africa with a diversified portfolio of mining and steelmaking assets "including Sesa Iron Ore, ESL Steel Limited, and Western Cluster Limited in Liberia, alongside associated industrial businesses".
- Credit rating stated as CRISIL AA / Stable.
- Recognitions cited include the Mormugao Port Authority award for highest export cargo tonnage, Best Safety & Health Culture of the Year (Minerals & Mining Conclave 2026 / ASSOCHAM), Gold Award at the 9th CII-IQ National Safety Practice Competition 2026, Platinum Award for Best Kaizen (Large Manufacturing), and Great Place to Work recognition in Mining & Quarrying for the 7th consecutive year.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Total net debt fell to ₹2,733 Cr in Jun'26 from ₹12,296 Cr in Mar'26; the net debt walk attributes the bulk to demerger adjustments of -9,788, leaving VISL net debt post-demerger of 2,508.
- "Net External Debt reduced to ₹1,773 Cr in Jun'26 from ₹2,862 Cr in Mar'26" and "Net External Debt / EBITDA stands at 1.3x in Q1 FY27" (stated as computed without considering inter-company loans of INR 960 Cr).
- Debt breakdown Jun'26 vs Mar'26 (₹ Cr): term debt 943 vs 1,161; short term borrowing 1,220 vs 2,919; working capital 629 vs 598; total consolidated debt 2,792 vs 4,678; cash and cash equivalents 1,018 vs 1,816; inter-company debt 960 vs 9,434.
- Cash & cash equivalents of ₹1,018 crore include restricted FDs of ₹352 Cr; ROCE stated as 16%, "computed basis equity + net debt".
- Finance cost fell 55% YoY from ₹461 crore to ₹207 crore "primarily on account of reduced debt, pre and post demerger" / "settlement of Inter-company payables as per group Demerger adjustments"; CFO cites "disciplined capital allocation".

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] The company was demerged effective 1 May 2026; every operational and financial slide carries the note that "the data presented in this slide covers the full quarter commencing 1 April 2026 and is not limited to the period following the demerger".
- [Ticker identity] The deck is Vedanta Iron And Steel Limited, not the business the VISL ticker may otherwise suggest; NSE Scrip Code VISL, and the deck contradicts itself on the BSE code — the covering letter states "BSE Scrip Code: 544784" while the About section states "(BSE: 544787 NSE: VISL)".
- [Market outlook] India's per capita steel consumption is shown at 102 kg vs a world average of 215 kg and China 601 kg (CY24); India steel production rises 120/127/144/152/168 Mn T over FY22-FY26 to 255 Mn T in FY31, and iron ore production 251/255/278/289/310 to 437* Mn T (estimated) in FY31, with the deck stating Indian steel production is "projected to grow at a CAGR of 8.7%" creating "a supply gap... creating significant headroom for further expansion in iron ore production".
- [Working capital] "Working capital increase reflects strategic inventory build-up ahead of the monsoon season, which will be released by Q2'27"; monsoon-related preparedness also lowered mine production and dispatches QoQ.
- [Deck error] The Earnings Call Details slide (page 25) is headed "Vedanta Power Limited" and branded "vedanta power" inside a Vedanta Iron & Steel presentation; the earnings call was scheduled for July 30, 2026, 5:00-6:30 PM IST.
